title: Crime Busters B 2027
summary: Crime Busters is a lab event: identify unknowns, analyse physical evidence, and write an analysis that names the culprit AND says why each other suspect was excluded. Half the score is the qualitative analysis, and the rules name every substance that can appear.
objectives: Identify any of the thirteen named solids, six metals and six liquids from solubility, acidity, magnetism, density, odour and the iodine and HCl tests
Work out the components of a two or three material mixture from test results
Identify the seven named recyclable plastics, and classify hair and fibres to the level the rules ask for
Run a paper chromatogram and compute an Rf that identifies a component
Read fingerprints, DNA electropherograms, prints, soil and spatter as evidence
Write an analysis that implicates one suspect with named evidence and excludes the rest with reasons

units.title: How a Scene Is Worked
units.summary: Twenty-five percent of the score is the written analysis, and it must say why each suspect was excluded as well as who did it.
objectives: State what evidence can and cannot establish
Write an analysis that excludes suspects with reasons

lessons.title: Every Contact Leaves a Trace
lessons.objective: State Locard's exchange principle and give an example of transfer evidence for each of hair, fibre and soil.

lessons.title: Class Evidence and Individual Evidence
lessons.objective: Classify a piece of evidence as class or individual characteristic evidence, and say what conclusion each will and will not support.

lessons.title: Chain of Custody and Contamination
lessons.objective: Describe what a chain of custody records and name three ways evidence is contaminated in collection or handling.

lessons.title: Writing the Analysis: Who, and Why Not the Others
lessons.objective: Write a crime scene analysis that links named evidence to a named suspect and states, for each other suspect, the evidence that excludes them.

lessons.title: Goggles, Waste and the Equipment List
lessons.objective: State the safety clothing the rules require, and explain what happens to a team that brings equipment not on the list.

units.title: The Tests You Run on an Unknown
units.summary: Half the score. Solubility, acidity, magnetism, colour, density and odour, plus the two reagents the supervisor always provides.
objectives: Choose a test that distinguishes two candidate solids
Read a test result correctly, including a negative

lessons.title: Solubility: Dissolves, Partly, or Not at All
lessons.objective: Run and read a solubility test in water, and use solubility alone to split the solids list into groups.

lessons.title: Acid, Base or Neutral
lessons.objective: Determine whether an unknown is acidic, basic or neutral using an indicator, and interpret the result for each named liquid.

lessons.title: The Iodine Test and What Turns Blue-Black
lessons.objective: Predict and explain the iodine result for each solid on the list, and name exactly which ones contain starch.

lessons.title: Adding HCl: Fizzing, Dissolving, Nothing
lessons.objective: Predict the result of adding 1M HCl to each named solid and metal, and name the gas produced in each case.

lessons.title: Magnetism, Lustre and Telling Six Metals Apart
lessons.objective: Distinguish aluminium, iron, zinc, magnesium, copper and tin using magnetism, colour, density and reaction with acid.

lessons.title: Density, Colour, Texture and Odour
lessons.objective: Estimate density from mass and volume, and record colour, crystal form, texture and odour as evidence rather than impression.

lessons.title: The Named Solids and How Each One Behaves
lessons.objective: For each of the thirteen solids the rules list, state its appearance and its result on the solubility, iodine and acid tests.

lessons.title: The Six Liquids
lessons.objective: Identify lemon juice, isopropyl alcohol, household ammonia, water, vinegar and hydrogen peroxide by odour, pH and reaction.

lessons.title: When the Container Holds Two or Three Things
lessons.objective: Work out which materials are present in a mixture from a set of test results, and explain why one positive result does not exclude the others.

units.title: Polymers, Hair and Fibres
units.summary: Ten percent of the score. The rules stop at animal/vegetable/synthetic for fibres and human/dog/cat for hair, and at seven named plastics.
objectives: Identify the seven recyclable plastics from density and burn data
Tell human from dog and cat hair under a microscope

lessons.title: Monomers, Polymers and Why Plastics Differ
lessons.objective: Define a polymer and explain how chain structure produces the density and melting differences that identify a plastic.

lessons.title: PETE, HDPE, PS, LDPE, PP, PVC and PMMA
lessons.objective: Identify each of the seven plastics named in the rules using a differential density test and a provided burn result.

lessons.title: Human, Dog or Cat
lessons.objective: Distinguish human, dog and cat hair by the cuticle, cortex and medulla features visible under a microscope.

lessons.title: Animal, Vegetable or Synthetic
lessons.objective: Classify a fibre as animal, vegetable or synthetic from its appearance and its burn behaviour, without naming the specific fibre.

units.title: Paper Chromatography and Rf
units.summary: Five percent of the score, and the chromatogram is collected with the score sheet.
objectives: Compute and use an Rf value

lessons.title: Why the Spots Move Different Distances
lessons.objective: Explain separation in terms of the mobile and stationary phases and the differing affinity of each component.

lessons.title: Running It Without Ruining It
lessons.objective: Set up a paper chromatogram with the origin above the solvent, and name the three mistakes that make a chromatogram unreadable.

lessons.title: Computing and Comparing Rf
lessons.objective: Compute an Rf from measured distances and explain why Rf identifies a component while raw distance does not.

units.title: Fingerprints, DNA, Prints, Soil and Spatter
units.summary: Ten percent of the score, across five kinds of evidence the rules name. No calculations are expected for prints or spatter.

lessons.title: Whorls, Loops and Arches
lessons.objective: Classify a fingerprint as a whorl, a loop or an arch, and state why fingerprints are individual rather than class evidence.

lessons.title: Comparing DNA Profiles
lessons.objective: Compare electropherograms from a scene and from suspects, and state what a shared peak and a missing peak each mean.

lessons.title: Prints, Treads, Direction and Speed
lessons.objective: Read direction and relative speed of travel from a print pattern, and compare a questioned print with a known one.

lessons.title: Soil as Evidence
lessons.objective: Compare scene soil with soil from a suspect using texture, colour and mineral composition, and say what a match does and does not establish.

lessons.title: Reading a Spatter Pattern
lessons.objective: Determine direction and relative impact speed from spatter shape and distribution, without calculation.
